newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINA, BRAZIL TO OPEN UP ELECTRICITY MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINA, BRAZIL TO OPEN UP ELECTRICITY MARKET.

text.p: Argentina and Brazil will open their electricity markets to free competition under an agreement due to be signed later Wednesday in Buenos Aires.

A memorandum of understanding seeks to guarantee fair trade, "without the application of subsidies which could alter normal competition and with prices that reflect efficient economic costs, avoiding discriminatory practices in supply and demand in both countries."
Under the agreement, released to the press by the Foreign Ministry, Brazilian firms and will be able to buy power from Argentine distributors, and vice versa.
Distributors in each country will also be able to choose their suppliers freely. They were restricted previously to buying from local providers.

The agreement was signed one month before Brazil awards a tender to purchase 1,000 megawatts of Argentine energy. The winning bidder will have to invest $200 million to build a conversion plant, according to local media reports.

The energy memorandum, set to be signed by Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella and Brazilian Ambassador Luis Seixas Correa, is seen as a stepping stone towards the integration of the two countries' natural gas markets.

It further stipulates "the need to develop a communications infrastructure to facilitate the exchange of data and information on the markets and to utilize any surplus in production, thus lowering energy prices."
Surplus energy would come chiefly from Brazil's dams and Argentina's thermoelectric plants.
